review.overview: PR #403 (feat: stage shared Railway queue) adds a new workspace package, @package/queue, and moves the scraper's queue handling onto it. The package defines typed queues behind a transport-independent contract. It has two adapters: a BullMQ/ioredis adapter for production and an in-memory adapter for tests. A shared contract test suite runs against both adapters, and a Redis-backed integration test runs against a real Redis process. The scraper's queues.ts now builds the scraper-items and scraper-images queues through this package. Its processor and producers use the portable enqueueMany, process, redriveFailed and counts calls instead of BullMQ objects. The scraper no longer depends on bullmq directly. It keeps its own Redis connection for cron checkpoints. On the infrastructure side, .railway/railway.ts declares a second Redis resource, pocket-trash-queue, next to the legacy scraper-queue. The new resource enables RDB and AOF persistence. Both resources stay in the project, and the docs describe the removal of scraper-queue as a later, separately approved stage. The docs also say the preview workflow keeps using scraper-queue until cutover. Supporting changes cover Railpack install configuration, Railway upload-context checks, CI Redis installation, change classification, and docs. The docs describe a Discord bot that will share the new Redis; the bot's code is not in this PR's file list.

changedAreas.summary: Adds @package/queue with a typed queue contract covering enqueue, enqueueMany, process, processContinuously, redriveFailed, counts, lifecycle events and close. Definitions carry a payload schema, worker mode, retry and retention settings, and completed-job deduplication policy. It includes a BullMQ/ioredis adapter and a deterministic in-memory adapter. It also includes a shared contract test suite, an in-memory contract test, and a real-Redis integration test. Its package.json lists bullmq, ioredis and zod as dependencies.

apps/scraper/src/queue/queues.ts is rewritten to create the scraper-items and scraper-images queues through createBullMqQueueAdapter or an injected QueueAdapter. It holds a shared retry and retention policy and zod payload schemas for item and image jobs. It exposes enqueueScraperJobs, getScraperQueueJobCounts and hasActionableQueueJobs. processor.ts replaces its drain and dead-letter helpers with queue.process and queue.redriveFailed, and drops the Redis connection option and direct BullMQ imports.

The Autmog and Grimsmo producers now enqueue QueueEnqueueInput batches through enqueueScraperJobs. jobs.ts calls createScraperQueues(env.REDIS_URL) and keeps its own Redis connection for scraper-owned cron checkpoints. job-ids.ts and scraper-types.ts have one-line changes. The scraper package.json swaps its bullmq dependency for @package/queue. Test files for producers, queues, jobs, env and cli are updated to match.

.railway/railway.ts renames the existing Redis variable to legacyScraperQueue and keeps scraper-queue with its current start command. It adds pocket-trash-queue with RDB (save 60 1) plus AOF (appendonly yes, appendfsync everysec) and a private endpoint named pocket-trash-queue. Both Redis resources are listed in the project, along with the scraper and redis-volume. The scraper's watched paths gain railpack.json and scripts/pnpm-install.sh.

Adds railpack.json, which runs scripts/pnpm-install.sh with --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline as the install step. deploy.yml sets RAILPACK_INSTALL_CMD on the preview and production scraper services. .railwayignore now allows railpack.json, scripts/pnpm-install.sh and packages/queue/**. check-railway-context.mjs and its test are updated; the fixture's expected tracked-file count changes from 14 to 16.

ci.yml gains a step that installs redis-server before tests. classify-changes.mjs adds a shared-queue category for packages/queue/ mapped to the scraper, preview and validation domains. It also adds railpack.json and scripts/pnpm-install.sh to the railway category. The matching tests in change-classification.test.mjs and railway-config.test.mjs are extended.

Adds the decision record eng-497-shared-queue-boundary.md, which describes the transport-independent boundary and at-least-once delivery. railway.md adds a staged shared-Redis migration sequence and states that the preview workflow keeps using scraper-queue until cutover. It also documents the REDIS_URL reference for the scraper and Discord bot, and the persistence and retention figures. environment-variables.md adds the /apps/discord-bot path and the shared Redis reference. complete-erasure.md adds rows for Discord notification jobs, ticket-operation records and the Axiom cursor. The two infrastructure-diagram files add queue nodes and edges for prod, preview and dev, plus the @package/queue workspace link.

Two changesets are added. One marks @package/queue as minor and @app/scraper as patch for shared typed queues and scraper delivery migration. The other marks @app/scraper as patch for staging the shared queue with RDB and AOF while retaining the legacy queue.

review.overview: PR #354 (feat(database): add Pens catalog schema) adds a Pens catalog domain to the @package/database Drizzle schema. A new file, packages/database/src/schema/pens.ts, defines 46 tables, all listed in the `pensTables` registry. They fall into these groups: Pen and refill subtype tables that share the product primary key; terminology concepts with role and nose-profile assignments; product configuration slots, choices, rules and requirements; refill offerings with tip style, ink color, identifiers, market status and compatibility groups; compatibility assertions and evidence; markets and source provenance; and owned-item detail tables for collections. The migration 20261010021729_pens_catalog_schema creates these tables. It also seeds lookup rows, backfills catalog_terminology_alias.concept_id, adds collection_item.serial_number, and defines plpgsql validation functions with triggers. collection.ts re-keys catalog_terminology_alias onto catalog_terminology_concept and adds composite unique keys on product, product_material and finish_option. relations.ts adds relation definitions, and index.ts exports two new row types. The catalog service switches alias writes and reads to the concept table. Tests include a new Pens integration suite, and the schema diagram HTML is updated. The diagrams show the domain map, then two ER slices: Pen subtypes with configuration, and refill offerings with compatibility, markets and evidence.

changedAreas.summary: New product subtype table marking complete pen products with temporal tracking. Shares primary key with product table via cascade delete.
Six interlinked tables forming pen part taxonomy: base part marker, plus concrete subtypes for clip, tip, top-cap, mechanism, and actuator. Each subtype references both product and base part tables.
Refill product detail with maker-model identity, normalized model text, and composite foreign key enforcing maker consistency with parent product.
Six collection detail tables for owned pen items. Pen detail tracks installed refill product and offering; part details link owned items to catalog products.
Ordered independently selected dimension for configurable products. Links to slot kind and product with position constraints.
Selectable option within a slot carrying exactly one carrier: material, finish option, or pen part. Enforced by carrier-valid check constraint.
OR-branch availability rule targeting a specific choice, with position-ordered requirements referencing earlier slots.
Hierarchical geographic scope with global, country, and region kinds. Code format validated by check constraints per kind.
External source identity linking maker, system, record ID, and URL. Unique identity constraint prevents duplicate listings.
Append-only evidence records supporting catalog claims with publisher, source kind, URL, capture date, and claim text. Protected by update/delete trigger.
Confirmed tip-size and ink-color combination for refill model. Composite unique key on refill product, tip style, normalized tip size, and ink color.
Versioned lifecycle state per market with successor chaining. Partial unique index ensures single active status per offering-market pair.
Versioned maker code or SKU with comparison rules, effective dates, and successor versioning. Supports trim normalization and custom comparison rules.
Physical interchangeability group backed by terminology concept. Groups refills that are mutually compatible.
Compatibility statement linking pen, optional required tip, and target refill or group. Outcome enum: compatible, incompatible, conditional, variable. Conditional outcomes require remedy text.
Structured evidence with kind-specific field validation via check constraint. Kinds: manufacturer-statement, dimensional-comparison, physical-fit-test, curated-observation.
Centralized canonical terminology with namespace-key uniqueness, label internationalization keys, and normalized label for search.
Functional role tags for pen parts linking to terminology concepts. Constrained to pen-part-role namespace.
Nose profile categorization for pens and pen tips. Constrained to pen-nose-profile namespace.
User-selected configuration choices with optional part installation. Foreign key validates choice belongs to slot and installed part matches choice part product.

Uses shared-primary-key pattern where detail tables inherit IDs from the base product table. Includes constraints enforcing that pen parts must have exactly one concrete subtype.

Six new collection detail tables for owned pens and pen parts. Collection items can have configuration selections that reference product configuration choices. Supports installed part references allowing owned parts to be installed in owned pens.

Refill compatibility groups for physical interchangeability, compatibility assertions linking pens to compatible refills with outcomes (compatible, incompatible, conditional, variable), and structured evidence tracking with four evidence kinds: manufacturer-statement, dimensional-comparison, physical-fit-test, and curated-observation.

Canonical terminology concepts with namespaces for product types, pen part roles, pen nose profiles, and refill compatibility groups. Market hierarchy with global, country, and region levels supporting directed containment edges.

Added 80+ new Drizzle relations covering pen products, collection details, configuration, refills, compatibility, terminology, markets, and source evidence. Relations support one-to-many and many-to-many relationships with proper foreign key mappings.

review.overview: PR #376 adds material drill-downs to the public Trends page. Two data sources feed them. The first is an exact count of approved, non-private catalog products by material. The second is a privacy-transformed count of owned collection items and distinct collectors by material. The database package adds a table, public_collection_item_material_trend, and a column, has_suppressed_material_values, on public_trends_generation. The services package extends the trends service with getPublicCatalogMaterialTrends, getPublicCollectionMaterialTrends, and material aggregation inside refreshPublicCollectionItemTrends. Tests, stories, and a changeset cover the web, services, and database changes.
